correctness.rationale: Exact summation of the twelve displayed drifts leaves \(\Pi-\mu T-\pi_pS_f\), while the twelve additive Brownian terms combine into one Brownian motion of variance rate \(\sigma_\Sigma^2\). Variation of constants yields \(T-Y=-\pi_p e^{-\mu t}\int_0^t e^{\mu s}S_f(s)ds\). Any path that stays nonnegative therefore has \(0\le T(t)\le Y(t)\), but \(Y(t)\) is Gaussian with positive variance for every \(t>0\), giving the stated strictly positive lower bound. The source's later Itô formulas contain \(\sigma_i^2X_i^2\) and \(\sigma_iX_i dB_i\), confirming that those calculations use a different multiplicative diffusion.

value.rationale: Positivity is the foundational biological-feasibility premise for all twelve compartments and for the article's stationary-distribution and long-time stochastic arguments. The correction is not a cosmetic sign check: it gives a universal, parameter-explicit positive lower bound on failure of the claimed state space at every positive time and identifies why the published proof does not apply to the printed equation. This directly separates a biologically admissible multiplicative-noise formulation from the published additive one and is useful before any downstream threshold interpretation.
